Jason has 3 different pairs of trousers and 4 different shirts. Emily has 2 different pairs of trousers and 5 different shirts. Each person can make an outfit by choosing 1 pair of trousers and 1 shirt. Who has a larger number of possible outfits, and by how many?

questions.explanation: Calgary 5 pm → London midnight → Auckland 1 pm (next day).

questions.prompt: Four old units for capacity are: gill, pint, quart and peck. 4 gills equal 1 pint. 1 pint equals half a quart. 8 quarts equal 1 peck. How many gills equal 1 peck?
questions.explanation: 1 quart = 2 pints = 8 gills. 1 peck = 8 quarts = 64 gills.

questions.prompt: Four identical rectangles measuring 4 cm × 9 cm are arranged inside a larger square, leaving a square gap in the centre. What is the area of the gap?
questions.explanation: Outer square 13 × 13 = 169 cm². Four rectangles = 4 × 36 = 144 cm². Gap = 25 cm² (a 5 × 5 square).
